outages.place: Southern Odisha, including Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, Kandhamal, and Boudh
outages.affected: TPSODL, as reported by OdishaBytes and Odisha Ray on Nov 20, 2026, said it had restored electricity supply to 1,069,026 consumers (written as 10,69,026 in those reports) after Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur on Friday morning, achieving 98.68 percent restoration — nearly 99 percent — across its eight-district operational area within seven hours. Those reports said all six affected 33 kV feeders, all 19 affected 33/11 kV power substations, and all 42 affected power transformers were restored, and that 364 of 365 affected 11 kV feeders and 35,749 affected distribution transformers had been restored. District-wise restoration was reported as 99.76 percent in Ganjam, 99.53 percent in Koraput, 98.90 percent in Gajapati, 98.06 percent in Rayagada, 98.01 percent in Nabarangpur, 97.55 percent in Boudh, 94.23 percent in Kandhamal, and 100 percent in Malkangiri. TPSODL CEO Amit Kumar Garg, quoted in those reports, said the company had achieved nearly 99 percent restoration. An earlier Nov 20 Odisha Stand report from Berhampur said TPSODL had reported that Cyclone Akvan affected 1,083,348 consumers across its operational area, including 534,361 in Ganjam district and 123,252 in Nabarangpur district. Later articles, including an Odisha Diary report dated Nov 21 from Berhampur and earlier Nov 20 Odisha News Online coverage, described Garg visiting cyclone-affected areas of Ganjam to review restoration and restated the same 1,083,348 affected-consumer total, including the Ganjam and Nabarangpur district figures, but did not give a later remaining-outage count or a later restoration percentage after the 98.68 percent figure. No official remaining-outage count, and no official estimated time for full restoration of remaining customers, was stated in those later reports. A New Indian Express report updated at 3:39 a.m. IST Saturday, Nov 21 (4:09 p.m. CT Friday) said power supply was disrupted in parts of the state due to the storm, with restoration work underway on a war footing in several areas of northern Odisha, including Bhadrak, Balasore and Mayurbhanj. That report did not give an official remaining-outage count for those northern districts or a later TPSODL remaining-outage count. No later official remaining-outage count or official notice of full restoration from TPSODL, TPNODL, or the Odisha government was found as of 12:00 PM CT Saturday (11:30 p.m. IST Saturday, Nov 21).
outages.start: Morning of Nov 20, 2026 (IST), when Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur
outages.updated: Nov 20–21, 2026, TPSODL figures via OdishaBytes and Odisha Ray (Nov 20); earlier TPSODL affected total via Odisha Stand (Nov 20); CEO restoration review via Odisha Diary (Nov 21) and Odisha News Online (Nov 20), which restated the same affected total and did not give a later remaining-outage count; New Indian Express report updated 3:39 a.m. IST Saturday, Nov 21 (= 4:09 p.m. CT Friday), on restoration work in northern Odisha including Bhadrak, Balasore and Mayurbhanj, with no official customer count; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Saturday (11:30 p.m. IST Saturday), no later official remaining-outage count or official notice of full restoration from TPSODL, TPNODL, or the Odisha government found

outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including a large-scale overnight and morning attack on Nov 20 and further strikes reported on Nov 21
outages.affected: Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Facebook statement reported by Ukrinform at 6:22 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (10:22 a.m. CT), and by Ukrinform in English at 6:54 p.m. EET Saturday (10:54 a.m. CT), said that after the massive overnight attack on Nov 20, energy workers had managed to partially stabilize electricity supplies in the affected regions, but that enemy attacks were continuing, including deliberate strikes on energy facilities that had already been restored, and that constant air-raid alerts were significantly complicating and slowing repair work. As a result, the ministry said, the electricity supply situation in the regions may change rapidly. The ministry said that as of the evening of Nov 21, the most difficult situation remained in Odesa region, where repeated attacks on high-voltage transmission networks had caused large-scale power outages and triggered automatic protection systems. It warned that temporary voltage fluctuations or drops may occur when supply is restored. No official nationwide customer count was given in that Saturday evening statement. Ukrenergo, as reported by LB.ua at 6:43 p.m. EET Friday, Nov 20 (10:43 a.m. CT), by UNIAN at 7:18 p.m. and 8:55 p.m. EET Friday (11:18 a.m. and 12:55 p.m. CT), and by Ukrinform at 7:12 a.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (11:12 p.m. CT Friday), citing Ukrenergo's Telegram, said that on Saturday, Nov 21, planned electricity outages would be in effect around the clock in parts of the country: hourly outage schedules of 1.5 to 3 groups for all categories of consumers, and capacity-restriction schedules for industry. UNIAN, citing Ukrenergo, said those 1.5 to 3 queues for household consumers should correspond to outages of 6 to 12 hours. Those Saturday schedules remained the latest nationwide Ukrenergo schedule found at the time of this update (8:00 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21, which is 12:00 PM CT Saturday). Natalia Zabolotna, head of the Vinnytsia regional military administration, as reported by Ukrinform at 10:52 a.m. EET Saturday (2:52 a.m. CT) and by NV at 10:26 a.m. EET Saturday (2:26 a.m. CT), said a Russian attack on Saturday morning had damaged an energy-infrastructure facility in Vinnytsia and that part of the city was without electricity, with energy crews working to restore supply. No official customer count was given for Vinnytsia. No official nationwide customer count was found as of 12:00 PM CT Saturday (8:00 p.m. EET Saturday).
outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, Energy Ministry via Ukrinform 6:22 p.m. EET Saturday (= 10:22 a.m. CT) and Ukrinform English 6:54 p.m. EET Saturday (= 10:54 a.m. CT) on partial stabilization after the Nov 20 attack, continuing strikes, and the most difficult situation remaining in Odesa region as of Saturday evening; Ukrenergo Saturday Nov 21 all-day schedules via LB.ua 6:43 p.m. EET Friday (= 10:43 a.m. CT), UNIAN 7:18 p.m. and 8:55 p.m. EET Friday (= 11:18 a.m. and 12:55 p.m. CT), and Ukrinform 7:12 a.m. EET Saturday (= 11:12 p.m. CT Friday), which remained the latest nationwide schedules found; Vinnytsia OVA head Natalia Zabolotna via Ukrinform 10:52 a.m. EET Saturday (= 2:52 a.m. CT) and NV 10:26 a.m. EET Saturday (= 2:26 a.m. CT) on a Saturday morning strike that left part of Vinnytsia without power; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Saturday (8:00 p.m. EET Saturday), no official nationwide customer count and no later official change to those Saturday schedules found

outages.cause: Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including a large-scale overnight and morning attack on Nov 20. On Saturday, Nov 21, DTEK said emergency outages had again been introduced, on Ukrenergo's order, in Dnipro city and in the Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, Pavlohradskyi, and Kamianskyi districts, and that hourly schedules did not apply there
outages.affected: Ukrinform, in a report published at 10:36 a.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (2:36 a.m. CT), citing DTEK Group in Telegram, said emergency electricity outages had been introduced in Dnipropetrovsk region on Ukrenergo's order. It said the emergency outages were in effect in Dnipro and in the Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, Pavlohradskyi, and Kamianskyi districts, and that during emergency outages the hourly schedules did not apply. Censor.NET, in a 10:49 a.m. EET Saturday report (2:49 a.m. CT) also citing DTEK, gave the same list of places and likewise quoted DTEK as saying that during emergency outages the schedules do not apply, and that the company would report any changes in its Telegram channel. MIC (mis.dp.ua), citing DTEK Dniprovski Elektromerezhi in a Saturday report, likewise said emergency outages were in effect that day in Dnipro and in those four districts, meaning without forecast hourly schedules, and that for the rest of the region, on Ukrenergo's order, stabilization (scheduled) outages had been introduced. Dnipro.media, as relayed by UKR.NET and timed at 3:45 p.m. EET Saturday (7:45 a.m. CT), said DTEK had published an updated Saturday hourly outage schedule for certain queues of DTEK Dniprovski Elektromerezhi customers in Dnipropetrovsk region. That schedule update did not itself state that the Saturday emergency outages in Dnipro and the four districts had been cancelled. No later official DTEK statement clearly cancelling those Saturday emergency outages was found as of 12:00 PM CT Saturday (8:00 p.m. EET Saturday). No official customer count for Dnipro or Dnipropetrovsk region was given in those Saturday statements. The latest official customer count found remains DTEK's Tuesday-morning figure. Suspilne, citing DTEK's Telegram page in an 11:18 a.m. EET Tuesday, Nov 17 report, said that after new large-scale Russian strikes on the region's energy infrastructure that morning, significant damage to energy facilities left 700,000 homes without power in Dnipro and the Dniprovskyi, Pavlohradskyi, Kamianskyi, and Samarivskyi districts. Censor.NET, also citing DTEK in an 11:22 a.m. Tuesday report, said 700,000 families were left without power in the region and likewise named those districts. No official restoration time was given. No later official customer count after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure was found as of 12:00 PM CT Saturday (8:00 p.m. EET Saturday).

outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, DTEK via Ukrinform 10:36 a.m. EET Saturday (= 2:36 a.m. CT) and Censor.NET 10:49 a.m. EET Saturday (= 2:49 a.m. CT) on Saturday emergency outages in Dnipro and four districts, with hourly schedules not applying; MIC, citing DTEK Dniprovski Elektromerezhi, on the same Saturday emergency-outage list and on scheduled outages for the rest of the region; Dnipro.media via UKR.NET 3:45 p.m. EET Saturday (= 7:45 a.m. CT) on an updated hourly schedule for certain DTEK queues, which did not itself state that those emergency outages had been cancelled; Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure, DTEK via Suspilne and Censor.NET; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Saturday (8:00 p.m. EET Saturday), no later official customer count after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure, and no later official DTEK statement clearly cancelling the Saturday emergency outages, found

outages.place: Odesa and parts of Odesa district
outages.cause: Repeated Russian attacks on high-voltage transmission networks, including a strike on a DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi energy facility on the morning of Nov 20. Ukraine's Energy Ministry said that as of the evening of Nov 21, those attacks were causing large-scale power outages in the region and triggering automatic protection systems
outages.affected: Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Facebook statement reported by Ukrinform at 6:22 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (10:22 a.m. CT), by LB.ua at 6:09 p.m. EET Saturday (10:09 a.m. CT), and by Suspilne at 5:14 p.m. EET Saturday (9:14 a.m. CT), said that as of the evening of Nov 21 the situation in Odesa region remained difficult. The ministry said repeated Russian attacks on high-voltage, or main, transmission networks had caused large-scale power outages across the region and triggered automatic protection systems, and it warned that temporary voltage fluctuations or drops may occur when supply is restored. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa regional military administration, as reported by Ukrinform and by RBC-Ukraine at 7:30 p.m. EET Saturday (11:30 a.m. CT), said electricity supplies in the region remained unstable after the massive attack on the energy system, and that power outages had been occurring throughout Saturday in parts of Odesa district, including the city of Odesa, because of attacks on high-voltage transmission networks. Kiper said that when electricity is unavailable, boiler houses and pumping stations may be temporarily suspended, that they are switched to backup power where technically possible, and that disruptions to heating and water supplies remain possible. No official Saturday evening customer count was given in those ministry or regional-administration statements. Earlier Friday, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in an official Nov 20 evening statement, said 8,000 families in 21 settlements remained without power after the morning attack, and that crews would work overnight to restore power to another 15,600 families in 55 villages and towns after weather-damage cleanup; earlier Friday morning, 41,000 households were without power in the Odesa and Rozdilna districts, according to DTEK's press service as reported by Ukrainska Pravda and Ekonomichna Pravda. KyivPost, at 11:45 a.m. EET Saturday (3:45 a.m. CT), citing DTEK, had said emergency outages introduced on Saturday morning in Odesa and part of Odesa district were later cancelled, with a return to stabilization schedules. The later Saturday evening Energy Ministry and Kiper statements are the latest official status found. No official Saturday remaining-customer count was found as of 12:00 PM CT Saturday (8:00 p.m. EET Saturday).
outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, Energy Ministry via Ukrinform 6:22 p.m. EET Saturday (= 10:22 a.m. CT), LB.ua 6:09 p.m. EET Saturday (= 10:09 a.m. CT), and Suspilne 5:14 p.m. EET Saturday (= 9:14 a.m. CT) on large-scale Saturday evening outages in Odesa region after repeated strikes on high-voltage transmission networks; Oleh Kiper, Odesa regional military administration, via Ukrinform and RBC-Ukraine 7:30 p.m. EET Saturday (= 11:30 a.m. CT) on outages throughout Saturday in parts of Odesa district, including the city of Odesa, and on possible heating and water disruptions; earlier Friday official DTEK remaining 8,000 families after the morning attack and 15,600 weather-related restorations planned overnight; earlier Friday morning 41,000-household figure; KyivPost 11:45 a.m. EET Saturday (= 3:45 a.m. CT) on Saturday morning emergency outages later being cancelled; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Saturday (8:00 p.m. EET Saturday), no official Saturday remaining-customer count found

outages.cause: Russian attack that seriously damaged energy equipment in Sarny district. Rivneoblenergo said hourly outage schedules did not apply because this was an emergency outage from the damage
outages.affected: Oleksandr Koval, head of the Rivne regional military administration, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 1:04 a.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (5:04 p.m. CT Friday), said that as a result of a Russian attack on Sarny district in Rivne region, 50 settlements had been left without electricity, and that constant air-raid alerts were preventing energy workers from promptly repairing the damage. Interfax-Ukraine quoted Koval's Telegram post as saying, "Half a hundred settlements have been de-energized as a result of an enemy attack on Sarny district. Constant alerts do not allow energy workers to promptly eliminate the consequences of the strike." Rivne Vechirnie (Rivnepost), in a report published at 11:35 a.m. EET Saturday (3:35 a.m. CT), citing Rivneoblenergo, said that as a result of the Russian attack and serious damage to energy equipment, 46 settlements in Sarny district remained without electricity. It said the company's specialists had been working since the previous evening to restore supply, and that constant air-raid alerts were not allowing energy workers to promptly eliminate the consequences of the strike. Rivnenski Novyny, at 10:22 a.m. EET Saturday (2:22 a.m. CT), likewise citing the situation in Sarny district, said 46 settlements had been left without electricity, that Rivneoblenergo crews had been working since the previous evening, and that hourly outage schedules did not apply because this was an emergency de-energization from damaged energy equipment. No official customer count was given. No official firm restoration time was given. No later official remaining-settlement or customer count after the Saturday morning Rivneoblenergo figure of 46 settlements was found as of 12:00 PM CT Saturday (8:00 p.m. EET Saturday).
outages.start: Evening of Nov 20, 2026 (Kyiv time), according to Rivneoblenergo as reported by Rivnepost and Rivnenski Novyny
outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, Rivneoblenergo via Rivne Vechirnie (Rivnepost) 11:35 a.m. EET Saturday (= 3:35 a.m. CT) and Rivnenski Novyny 10:22 a.m. EET Saturday (= 2:22 a.m. CT) on 46 settlements in Sarny district still without power and on emergency rather than scheduled outages; Oleksandr Koval, Rivne regional military administration, via Interfax-Ukraine 1:04 a.m. EET Saturday (= 5:04 p.m. CT Friday) on 50 settlements; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Saturday (8:00 p.m. EET Saturday), no later official remaining-settlement or customer count and no official firm restoration time found

outages.place: Kurdistan Region, including Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Duhok, Bazian, and Chamchamal
outages.cause: Suspected drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field on the night of Nov 8, 2026, which halted gas production that supplies much of the region's electricity generation. Dana Gas, the field's operator, later said the facility had sustained significant damage and could produce no gas
outages.affected: Al Jazeera, on Nov 9, 2026, citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials, said a Sunday-night drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field caused a fire and left more than 70 percent of the Kurdish region without power. Omid Ahmed (also spelled Omed Ahmed), spokesperson for the Kurdistan Regional Government's Ministry of Electricity, said the attack suspended gas supply to power plants in Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Bazian, Chamchamal, and Duhok, and knocked between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts of generation off the grid, Al Jazeera reported, citing the official Iraqi News Agency (INA). Rudaw later quoted Ahmed as saying that authorities had increased generation from approximately 1,000 megawatts immediately after the attack to 1,550 megawatts, of which 50 megawatts were reserved for essential facilities and factories, leaving 1,500 megawatts for residents and raising daily public electricity supply to six to eight hours, reaching nine hours in some areas. Ahmed said the electricity then available covered only 40 percent of the region's demand, leaving a 60 percent shortfall, and that no date had been established for production to resume. Rudaw's article image assets for that report are dated Nov 13, 2026. Dana Gas, in a Saturday statement reported by Rudaw, said the facility had sustained significant damage and that currently no amount of gas could be produced. 964media, in a Nov 15 report, quoted Ahmed as saying that no timeframe had been set for electricity supplies to return to normal and that the ministry was waiting for gas from Khor Mor to flow again; in that interview he also said that within 48 hours of the attack the ministry had increased generation from 1,000 megawatts to nearly 1,650 megawatts, and that some areas were then getting more than eight hours of grid power a day, particularly on holidays. The same report said grid supply had fallen to three to four hours a day right after the attack and was later raised to six to seven hours, and that Dana Gas had said the field could produce no gas. No official customer count was given. No later official generation figure, public-supply-hours update, or official confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed was found as of 12:00 PM CT Saturday, Nov 21.
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. As of the latest official statements found, no date had been established for Khor Mor production to resume.
outages.updated: Nov 8–16, 2026 attack and aftermath: Al Jazeera Nov 9 citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials and INA; KRG electricity ministry figures via Rudaw (article image assets dated Nov 13); Dana Gas still-shut statement via Rudaw and 964media; Omed Ahmed via 964media Nov 15 on no timeframe for a return to normal supply and on generation rising to nearly 1,650 megawatts within 48 hours of the attack; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Saturday, Nov 21, no later official generation figure or confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed found

outages.place: Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Horlivka, Yenakiieve, Debaltseve, Snizhne, and nearby districts
outages.cause: Local accidents and a power deficit, according to the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, including a Friday evening equipment failure in Donetsk, and a later Saturday evening disruption that the ministry attributed to combat in a neighboring region
outages.affected: The occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, in a Saturday evening statement reported by RIA Novosti at 8:35 p.m. Saturday, Nov 21 (11:35 a.m. CT if the time is Moscow time), said that as a result of combat actions by Ukrainian forces in a neighboring region, electricity supply had been disrupted in a way that affected part of the occupied Donetsk region's territory. The ministry said the list of urban and municipal districts without electricity, and the scale of the damage in the neighboring region, were still being clarified. It also said that in Donetsk city, energy workers were continuing work to reconnect consumers left without power after an accident, and that some subscribers had already been reconnected. That Saturday evening statement did not give a new official region-wide remaining-customer count. The latest official region-wide remaining total found remains the occupation ministry's Saturday morning figure. The ministry, in a Saturday morning statement reported by DNR News at 10:12 a.m. Saturday (1:12 a.m. CT if Moscow time), and citing Donetskenergo, said that as of 7:00 a.m. Saturday, Nov 21 (10:00 p.m. CT Friday if that time is Moscow time), more than 107,000 subscribers in the occupied region remained without power. The same Saturday morning statement said that around 7:00 p.m. Friday, Nov 20 (10:00 a.m. CT Friday if Moscow time), a failure in electrical-network equipment had left part of Donetsk without electricity, and that partial outages also continued in Makiivka, Mariupol, Yenakiieve, Horlivka, Debaltseve, and the Yasynuvata, Amvrosiivka, Volnovakha, Telmanove, and Volodarske municipal districts because of a shortage of available capacity and local emergency situations. Occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin, as reported by News.ru at 11:42 a.m. Saturday (2:42 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said more than 67,000 subscribers in Donetsk remained without power because of network overloads and emergency outages. No later official region-wide remaining total after the 7:00 a.m. Saturday figure of more than 107,000 subscribers was found as of 12:00 PM CT Saturday (9:00 p.m. Moscow time Saturday).
outages.start: Around 7:00 p.m. Friday, Nov 20, 2026 (10:00 a.m. CT Friday if Moscow time), for the Donetsk city equipment failure described by the occupation ministry; other partial outages in the region were already being reported
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. The Saturday evening occupation-ministry statement said the list of affected districts and the scale of the neighboring-region damage were still being clarified, and that reconnection work was continuing in Donetsk city.
outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy via RIA Novosti 8:35 p.m. Saturday (= 11:35 a.m. CT if Moscow time) on a Saturday evening supply disruption affecting part of the occupied region after combat in a neighboring region, with the list of districts and the scale still being clarified, and on continued reconnection work in Donetsk city; earlier Saturday morning official region-wide remaining total of more than 107,000 subscribers as of 7:00 a.m. Saturday, occupation ministry via DNR News 10:12 a.m. Saturday (= 1:12 a.m. CT if Moscow time), citing Donetskenergo; occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin via News.ru 11:42 a.m. Saturday (= 2:42 a.m. CT if Moscow time) on more than 67,000 subscribers remaining without power in Donetsk; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Saturday (9:00 p.m. Moscow time Saturday), no later official region-wide remaining total after the 7:00 a.m. Saturday figure of more than 107,000 subscribers found

outages.place: Crimea, including Dzhankoy, Yevpatoria, and Bilohirsk
outages.cause: A power-capacity shortage and consumption restrictions introduced on Saturday, Nov 21, on orders of the Russian federal System Operator, according to Krymenergo. Occupation sources have said peninsula-wide interruptions began after strikes on transmission networks outside the peninsula on Oct 24, 2026
outages.affected: Krymenergo, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea at 11:40 a.m. Saturday, Nov 21 (2:40 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said that on Saturday six districts and three cities on the peninsula were without power, for an estimated three hours, because of introduced restrictions on electricity supply. It said residents were without power in villages of the Rozdolne, Sovietskyi, Saky, Pervomaiske, Kirovske, and Dzhankoy districts, that 75 streets and lanes in Dzhankoy were without power, that 36 streets in Yevpatoria were without power, and that 44 streets and three garden partnerships in Bilohirsk were without power. The same report said consumption-mode restrictions had been introduced on Saturday and that lights would be turned off in populated places for three to six hours. An earlier Krymenergo statement, reported by RIA Novosti Crimea at 9:06 a.m. Saturday (12:06 a.m. CT if Moscow time) and by News-CR at 8:51 a.m. Saturday (11:51 p.m. CT Friday if Moscow time), said the Saturday restrictions were introduced on orders of the Russian federal System Operator, that the approximate duration of the outages was 3 to 6 hours, that if the outage periods were extended or additional restrictions were introduced further information would be published, and that at that earlier hour power was already out in parts of Bilohirsk and the Rozdolne and Sovietskyi districts, with a planned restoration there in about three hours. No official customer count was given. Occupation sources have said peninsula-wide interruptions began Oct 24, 2026, after strikes on transmission networks outside the peninsula, and that additional restrictions followed a later attack on Nov 4. No later official notice that the Saturday restrictions had ended, been extended, or been replaced by a new official remaining-customer count was found as of 12:00 PM CT Saturday (9:00 p.m. Moscow time Saturday).
outages.start: Occupation sources said peninsula-wide interruptions began Oct 24, 2026; Saturday's additional 3-to-6-hour restrictions were reported Nov 21, 2026
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given for the Saturday restrictions as a whole. Krymenergo, as reported Saturday morning, said the approximate duration of the outages was 3 to 6 hours and that further information would be published if the periods were extended or additional restrictions were introduced.
outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, Krymenergo via RIA Novosti Crimea 11:40 a.m. Saturday (= 2:40 a.m. CT if Moscow time) on six districts and three cities, including 75 streets and lanes in Dzhankoy, 36 streets in Yevpatoria, and 44 streets in Bilohirsk, and on Saturday 3-to-6-hour consumption restrictions; earlier Krymenergo via RIA Novosti Crimea 9:06 a.m. Saturday (= 12:06 a.m. CT if Moscow time) and News-CR 8:51 a.m. Saturday (= 11:51 p.m. CT Friday if Moscow time) on System Operator orders and on a planned restoration in about three hours for places already out that morning; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Saturday (9:00 p.m. Moscow time Saturday), no later official notice that the Saturday restrictions had ended or been extended, and no official customer count, found

outages.cause: Generation-capacity deficit in the national electric system. UNE's Saturday bulletin said unit 8 of CTE Mariel, units 1 and 2 of CTE Santa Cruz, and unit 2 of CTE Felton were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance, with thermal-generation limitations of 394 MW
outages.affected: UNE's Saturday bulletin, published by Cubadebate on Saturday, Nov 21, and also reported by Juventud Rebelde, which posted the same official figures at 8:36 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (7:36 a.m. CT) and updated the article at 8:54 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (7:54 a.m. CT), said the national electric system continued to face a generation-capacity deficit. It said service had been affected by a capacity deficit throughout all 24 hours on Friday, Nov 20, and that the affectation continued through the early morning, with a maximum affectation of 1,799 MW recorded at 7:10 p.m. Cuba time Friday (6:10 p.m. CT Friday). It said solar-photovoltaic parks produced 4,177 MWh, with a maximum of 650 MW delivered in the midday period. At 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Saturday, Nov 21 (5:00 a.m. CT), the bulletin said SEN availability was 980 MW against demand of 2,270 MW, with 1,295 MW affected. For the midday period it estimated an affectation of 1,400 MW. For the evening peak, UNE estimated that unit 8 of CTE Mariel would enter with 45 MW, and it forecast availability of 1,025 MW against a maximum demand of 2,800 MW, a deficit of 1,775 MW, and, if those conditions held, an affectation of 1,805 MW at the peak. Official UNE sources did not report a total collapse of the national grid. No official Saturday evening-peak actual from UNE was found as of 12:00 PM CT Saturday (1:00 p.m. Cuba time Saturday), before the evening peak.
outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, UNE Saturday bulletin via Cubadebate and Juventud Rebelde, posted 8:36 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (= 7:36 a.m. CT) and updated 8:54 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (= 7:54 a.m. CT), including the official Friday evening-peak actual of 1,799 MW at 7:10 p.m. Cuba time Friday (= 6:10 p.m. CT Friday), Saturday 6:00 a.m. Cuba time figures of 980 MW available, 2,270 MW demand, and 1,295 MW affected, and a Saturday evening-peak forecast affectation of 1,805 MW; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Saturday (1:00 p.m. Cuba time Saturday), no official Saturday evening-peak actual from UNE found

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. Drop Site News, in a Nov 20, 2026 report from Khartoum, said a particularly intense wave of drone strikes at the end of October and into November targeting power stations, fuel supplies, and electricity infrastructure had brought the country's power grid to the brink of collapse, and that two weeks after the wave of attacks, major substations remained out of service. Shaker Ismail, an engineer with the Sudanese Electricity Company, told Drop Site that repairing some of the country's most important power facilities could take months or longer, that high-capacity transformers and digital control systems had been damaged, and that replacement transformers must be manufactured to order abroad. Ismail said the Um Dabakir thermal power plant in White Nile State was badly damaged in an Oct 29 strike and forced to shut down, and that the Al-Markhiyat substation west of Omdurman was put out of service after an Oct 27 strike; he said affected areas continued to experience prolonged outages and scheduled power cuts as of this week. The report said the Sudan Electricity Holding Company and Ministry of Energy had yet to publicly announce the restoration of the major facilities damaged in the attacks. A United Nations report published Nov 17, issued in Geneva and posted on the UN in Sudan website, said that in just over two weeks between Oct 20 and Nov 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. An earlier Al Jazeera Nov 15 feature said there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day, and, citing The Associated Press, said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found as of 12:00 PM CT Saturday.
